title: Hesed: Faithful Love
lead: Hesed is loyal, generous love inside a relationship, love that keeps faith and often goes beyond what duty requires. It is one of the words God uses to describe himself (Exodus 34:6–7) and appears about 250 times in the Hebrew Bible, most often in the Psalms. The KJV usually renders it "mercy" or "lovingkindness."

sections.b:
God reveals himself to Moses as "great in loyal love and faithfulness" (Exodus 34:6–7), the loyal love being hesed, and Psalm 136 repeats "his hesed endures forever" 26 times. The prophets ask for it from people too: "Loyal love is what I want, not sacrifice" (Hosea 6:6; the Hebrew for "loyal love" is hesed), quoted by Jesus (Matthew 9:13), and "do justice, love hesed, and walk humbly with your God" (Micah 6:8).

Scholars debate its core meaning. Nelson Glueck argued that it is the loyalty owed within a covenant or relationship; Katharine Doob Sakenfeld and Gordon Clark argued that it is loyal kindness freely given, often by the stronger to the weaker, beyond any obligation. The Septuagint usually translates it eleos, "mercy."
sections.refs: Exodus 34:6–7; Psalm 136:1; Hosea 6:6; Micah 6:8; Matthew 9:13; Lamentations 3:22–23
